name: K-12 charter school
summary: Charter schools are typically 35k-90k SF one- or two-story buildings with standard classrooms, a combined gym/cafetorium, a serving kitchen and limited athletic facilities, often built design-build by charter networks or developers with leaner specs than district schools. No charter-specific cost dataset could be retrieved in this session, so the hard cost is DERIVED from state K-12 contract data (NC DPI 2024-25, ~$400-$480/SF incl. site) discounted for charter program and spec; verify against charter bond offering documents or network build costs.

typicalSize.method: Derived: charter campuses commonly serve 400-900 students at ~80-110 GSF/student (vs. ~120-150 for district schools; NC district elementary average ~122,000 SF per school in e1). Mid 55,000 SF ~ 550 students at 100 GSF/student.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Building SF per site acre: suburban charter elementary ~4-8 acres for 40-60k SF (~8,000-12,000 SF/acre); urban two-story campuses on 2-3 acres reach ~20,000 SF/acre. Derived.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Spaces per building SF (= 1.2-2.5 per 1,000 SF): ~1 per staff plus visitors, with a separate stacking lane for car-rider queue. Derived; local code governs.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived. Anchors (site + building contract cost): NC district elementary $421.62/SF and high $483.37/SF in 2025 (e1), all 2024 schools $452.05/SF with range $376-$526 (e2); VA classroom buildings $474/SF (2026, e3). Charter schools omit most district athletic facilities, auditoriums and stadium sitework, use smaller sites and simpler finishes, and are frequently design-build - taken as ~0.85 x the NC elementary average: 0.85 x $422 = ~$360/SF (2025). Low $260 ~ RSMeans/Gordian model-level building cost ($239 in 2024, e4) plus ~10% site = shell-and-classroom charter on a simple site; high $500 ~ district-equivalent spec / high-cost market (e1 high school, e3).

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. GC/OH&P and on-site work (parking, car-rider loop, play areas, utilities, landscaping); excludes land, soft costs, classroom furniture/technology (FF&E), athletic stadiums/turf fields, off-sites and impact/tap fees.

qualityTiers.method: Economy ~ model-level/simple charter ($260/$360 = 0.72); premium ~ district-standard elementary ($422-$452 / $360 = 1.17-1.26, e1/e2); luxury ~ high school / STEM-heavy campus (~$500/$360 = 1.39).

systemSplit.method: Derived from a typical one/two-story masonry-and-steel school: HVAC 12% (classroom ventilation rates), electrical 9% + communications 3% + security/fire alarm 2%, finishes 9%, site 10% (31-33). No public CSI-level charter or K-12 bid breakdown was retrieved in this session - replace with a state school-facility cost-model split when available.

lineItems.name: Gym / cafetorium (multi-purpose) incl. stage and gym equipment

cost.method: Derived allowance for fixed gym equipment, stage rigging/AV and folding tables in a combined gym/cafetorium (the room itself is in baseline building SF).
Derived: warming/serving line for satellite meals (low) to full production kitchen with hood and walk-ins (high).

lineItems.name: Playground equipment and natural-grass play field

cost.method: Derived allowance (K-5 playground with surfacing plus a graded/irrigated multi-use field).

lineItems.name: Synthetic turf athletic field with lighting
Secure entry vestibule, access control, cameras

cost.method: Derived allowance; many states now require secured vestibules for new schools.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived: classroom furniture, cafeteria tables, library/media and instructional technology ~$1,500-$3,500 per student at ~100 GSF/student. NC contract data excludes furnishings (e1), confirming FF&E sits outside hard cost.

pctOfHard.method: Derived. NC contract data explicitly excludes 'design fees, surveys, testing or legal expense' (e1); typical K-12 A/E 6%-8%, testing/inspection 1%-2%, survey/geotech/legal 1%-2%, owner's rep 2%-3%, permits 1%. Charter projects add bond/financing transaction costs (carried in financing, not here). Excludes FF&E and contingency.

softCosts.notes: Charter schools typically finance through tax-exempt conduit bonds; issuance costs, capitalized interest and debt-service reserve funds belong to financing.

design.method: Derived: repeatable network prototypes need less design contingency than bespoke district schools.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Low ~ $260 hard x 1.1; high ~ $500 hard x 1.3 + FF&E. Per student at ~100 GSF/student this is ~$28k-$70k per seat.

evidence.quote: Model page cost table (45,000 SF, 2019 data): SubTotal $143.83/SF; Contractor Fees 25%; Architectural Fees 7%; Total Building Cost $192.37/SF (union)
evidence.scopeNotes: Building only, union labor, 2019 national average; includes contractor GC/OH&P (25%) AND architect fees; excludes sitework, land, FF&E. Hard cost w/o A/E fee = SubTotal x 1.25. Stale (2019) and well below current bids; used for relative ratios between types only.

openQuestions: No charter-specific source was retrievable (search budget exhausted): pull charter school conduit bond official statements (EMMA) or network build budgets (IDEA, KIPP, Great Hearts, BASIS) for actual $/SF and $/seat.
State cost-cap data (Washington OSPI Construction Cost Allocation, Ohio OFCC, MSBA, Texas TABS charter registrations) would add independent anchors and a CSI split.
SF per student for charters (~80-110 GSF) is a derived assumption.
